\[
P=(X,Y) \qquad\text{with}\qquad Y=X^{2},
\]

and suppose the point is chosen uniformly along the portion of the curve
\(y=x^{2}\) for \(0<x<n\).  
Uniformity on the graph means that the \(x\)–coordinate is uniformly
distributed on the interval \((0,n)\).

---

### 1.  Distribution of \(X\)

\[
f_{X}(x)=\frac{1}{n},\qquad 0<x<n .
\]

---

### 2.  Expected \(x\)‑coordinate  

\[
E[X]=\int_{0}^{n}x\,f_{X}(x)\,dx
      =\frac{1}{n}\int_{0}^{n}x\,dx
      =\frac{1}{n}\Bigl[\frac{x^{2}}{2}\Bigr]_{0}^{n}
      =\frac{n}{2}.
\]

---

### 3.  Expected \(y\)‑coordinate  

Since \(Y=X^{2}\),

\[
E[Y]=E[X^{2}]=\int_{0}^{n}x^{2}f_{X}(x)\,dx
      =\frac{1}{n}\int_{0}^{n}x^{2}\,dx
      =\frac{1}{n}\Bigl[\frac{x^{3}}{3}\Bigr]_{0}^{n}
      =\frac{n^{2}}{3}.
\]

---

### 4.  Expected point  

The expected location (the vector expectation) of the random point on the
graph is therefore  

\[
E[(X,Y)]=\bigl(E[X],\,E[Y]\bigr)=\left(\frac{n}{2},\,\frac{n^{2}}{3}\right).
\]

\[
\boxed{\displaystyle \left(\frac{n}{2},\frac{n^{2}}{3}\right)}
\]<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
